methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
JetZero, a Series B transportation company founded by Tom O'Leary and Mark Page, has raised over $1.0B to date. The broader transportation sector includes 7 private peers (Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, The ePlane Company among others) and no direct public comparables, limiting traditional peer-based valuation approaches.

Given the scarcity of same-stage or valuation-tier comparable data in transportation, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology. Using the $1.0B total raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, this approach yields $1.9B. This method is applicable but represents a single triangulation point, as peer-median analysis could not be substantiated—only 3 same-sector peers exist, and none met the criteria for narrow-stage or valuation-tier filtering, making broad-sector median comparison unreliable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.6B to $2.2B (median $1.9B), derived from stage-progression with conservative and upside variants. The central uncertainty remains the absence of tight peer comparables at similar stage and scale. Refinement would require either narrowing to pure-play aerospace or aviation subsector peers, or obtaining additional market-based transaction data from the broader transportation frontier-tech cohort. Capital raised to date serves as the most concrete anchor point given current data constraints.
